### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItem))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItem))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItem))_

- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in saveMetaItem))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aa497a2e3109443cfe0a44332bf2d34e659089c6` — the merge of head `532985f37f9aa4460526df86699de0a4f7cbde91` into base `cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aa497a2e3109443cfe0a44332bf2d34e659089c6 && git checkout aa497a2e3109443cfe0a44332bf2d34e659089c6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23 532985f37f9aa4460526df86699de0a4f7cbde91 && git checkout -B drift-repro cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23 && git merge --no-ff 532985f37f9aa4460526df86699de0a4f7cbde91

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cdb949a288e1bd3350f09527c5f2169eb4752c23` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ef6a96021bda9ee4776a897e03c2528392afb20`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/draft-changes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-save-request.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDraftMark.tsx

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head at read time (2026-10-28): 46 runs; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards` are `success`; `Test Core (1-8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, every `Lint ·` lane (ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates, CI/release/engine gates, three scoped lanes) and every `Type Check ·` lane (workspace, debt ledger, source gates, consumer gates) are still **in progress**, so the derived gate families below (generated artifacts, strictness ledger, type-alias pin count, UI type check, changeset level) have no conclusion yet. The judgments here are read off the tree; the in-progress runs are the gate verdicts once they conclude.

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/api`** — `MetadataAuthoringSurfaceSchema` widens `['copilot','studio','api']` to `['copilot','mcp','studio','api']`; new export `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` / `MetadataAuthoringClient` (`{ id: string(min 1), name?: string(min 1) }`); `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.draftChanges[].client` optional; `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.client` optional. Every consumer of `MetadataAuthoringSurface` is a `z.infer` type (`DraftChange['by']`, `MetaSaveRequestMembers`, `MetadataClientSaveOptions`), so a widening that adds one enum member is additive and non-breaking. **Right.** The index re-exports `./protocol.zod` wholesale, so the new schema is published without an index edit. **Right.**
- **Accept set, in-process save** — `saveMetaItem` now accepts `surface: 'mcp'` (through `MetadataAuthoringSurfaceSchema.safeParse`, so the spec is the source) and `client` only beside `surface: 'mcp'`, refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` otherwise or malformed, before any read or write (`protocol.ts` ~20245, tested with `metadataWrites()` empty). **Right.**
- **Accept set, HTTP doors** — `metaSaveRequestOptions` (`packages/rest/src/meta-save-request.ts`) refuses `?surface=mcp` with its own sentence; `HTTP_SAVE_SURFACES` stays `['studio','api']`. Both doors spread `...saveOptions.request`, whose type `MetaSaveRequestMembers` is a `Pick` of exactly `parentVersion`, `mode` and `surface`, into a request built member by member (`meta-item-write-routes.ts` ~283-345; `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` ~1599-1612), so no wire `client` can reach the save. The describe's "no HTTP door reads it" claim holds in the tree. **Right.** The narrowed set the UI client may send (`MetadataClientSaveOptions.surface`, the spec's `by` set with `copilot` and `mcp` excluded) tracks the doors. **Right.**
- **Stored form and read** — `mergeDraftChanges` stamps `client` only when the stamp has one; `storedDraftChanges` admits `mcp` entries with or without a client and treats a client beside a non-`mcp` surface, or a malformed one, as malformed (whole `draftChanges` dropped, as for any bad entry today). The draft read serves the entries unchanged (`protocol.ts` ~10999 / ~11034), so a stored `client` reaches `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` and parses (pinned end-to-end in `protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`). **Right.**
- **Generated artifacts** — `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `authorable-surface` (`MetadataAuthoringClient:id/name`, `SaveMetaItemRequest:client`), `json-schema.manifest`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, references index and the untriaged `api/` strictness count 448 → 449 are all regenerated in the diff. The type-alias pin count 798 → 799 adds `Iso_api_protocol__MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` (no default, no transform; `z.input` equals `z.infer`). **Right**, pending the in-progress Lint/Type Check lanes.
- **ADR alignment** — ADR-0033's provenance item ("attribute each AI draft to the acting user + mark it AI-sourced") is carried at the key grain with `actor` unchanged and an added attribution member; ADR-0090 D10 rule 4 / ADR-0118 D1-D5 forbid moving `actor` and answer "which non-user acted" with an added field, which `client` is. No ADR is contradicted; none needs amending.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/27176-mcp-draft-provenance.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/rest` patch, `@object-ui/data-objectstack` / `app-shell` / `i18n` patch. Body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`; the PR body carries the same two lines. A new accepted enum member on a published authoring schema is `added`, which owes at least `minor` on at least one moved package (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, ruling A) — spec and metadata-protocol are the packages whose published source the kind moves, both minor; the HTTP doors and the console only track the set, patch. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition, no tombstone. **Level and both declaration lines match what the diff publishes.** `Check Changeset` is in progress; its conclusion is the gate verdict.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `open_questions` and no dev flag in the PR body or on the card.
- The cloud half (the MCP build door passing `surface: 'mcp'` and the verified client from its principal into the save) is declared as a follow-up on cloud#3302, which the card's "Done looks like" item 3 already scopes that way. Read in the cloud checkout: the door's tool context carries `authoringDoor: 'mcp'` and the execution context's `performedBy.clientId` (`assemble-execution-context.ts:352`); a registered display name must be read off `sys_oauth_application` by that door — the spec's `name` is "as registered, absent when none", which that producer can honour. Not a flag on this PR.
- The `@ts-expect-error` pin for `mcp` sits in `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/draftChanges-12725.test.ts` beside the existing `copilot` pin (same file, same compile program), so it is not a phantom check by the AGENTS.md test. UI remainder is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; `Type Check · consumer gates` answers it.
- Docblocks cite `[#27176]` the way the same file cites `[#24298]`; the `describe()` strings (runtime prose) carry no tracker number.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, judged against the card (attribution only: which door, which OAuth client, on whose behalf), ADR-0033 / ADR-0090 D10 rule 4, and its first consumers (the writer in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the two HTTP doors, `StudioDraftMark` / `DraftChangesPanel`, and the cloud MCP door to come).

Holds:
- Separating `by: 'mcp'` (the door) from `client` (the agent) from `actor` (the person) answers all three of the card's questions without a second actor vocabulary; two clients of one person on one draft are told apart by `client.id`, which is what the card asked for.
- `client` is server-stated like `writeFace`, and the tree keeps it so: the only two HTTP producers of `SaveMetaItemRequest` build it from a `Pick` that has no `client`; `?surface=mcp` is refused on both doors with the same mapping. An HTTP caller cannot label its write as an agent's, nor attribute it to another client.
- "Present only beside `by: 'mcp'`" is enforced where it can be: refused at the save and dropped as malformed at the stored read; the schema's prose matches the enforcement (Prime Directive #10).
- `name` optional with `min(1)` and "never the id standing in for it" is the right shape for Studio's line: `draftAgentText` renders the registered name or "an unnamed MCP client", never `client.id` (read in `StudioDraftMark.tsx:84-90`).
- `z.input` equals `z.infer`, so the new type carries no `…Parsed` twin; the pin count moves by one.

Tried to break it:
- A `client` on an active (`publish`) `mcp` save: accepted and recorded nowhere — stated in the describe, same posture as `surface` on an active save. Holds.
- A stored `mcp` entry whose `client` was later hand-edited beside `studio`: the read drops the whole `draftChanges` as malformed. Same as every other bad entry; holds.
- A wire body carrying `client` with `?surface=studio`: `item` is the body, the request is built member by member, `client` never read. Holds.

**Should-fix (not blocking):** the spec and the writer disagree on an unknown member. `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` is a plain `z.object`, so `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema.safeParse({ id: 'cli_1', secret: 's' })` succeeds and strips `secret`; `authoringClientOf` refuses the same value and the save answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` ("malformed"). The surface member is validated through the spec schema itself; the client member is validated by a hand-rolled check that is stricter than the published contract, which is the drift Prime Directive #12 warns against (one contract, owned at the spec). Either mark the schema `.strict()` (so the spec's own refusal is the one the writer applies, and the strictness ledger counts it as such) or have `authoringClientOf` parse through the spec schema; the test rows `an extra member` / `{ id, secret }` then pin the spec's verdict rather than a second one. Nit in the same file: `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema`'s own `.describe` says "(see `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema`)", a self-reference.

No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-e4rirs`
Reviewed-by: `session_0123kRqqdpAJWYMgsgdAJX4G`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b1028a55ae009cc51266f0696e29088d215d458`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/draft-changes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/spec/src/api/meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, packages/spec/json-schema.manifest/api.json, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/api.md

Delta review. This head is `6ef6a96021bda9ee4776a897e03c2528392afb20` plus one commit, `2b1028a55a` ("fix(spec): close MetadataAuthoringClientSchema and judge the save's client by it"), which touches four files. The `6ef6a96021` record (PASS, one should-fix, one nit) stands for everything the delta does not touch; the sections below judge the delta and restate only what it changes.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on `2b1028a55a` at read time: 23 runs; 4 `success`, 3 `skipped`, and 16 still **in progress** — every `Lint ·` lane, every `Type Check ·` lane, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected`, `Auto Label`. The Test Core shards and the Build jobs had not yet been planned on this head. The judgments below are read off the tree; the in-progress runs are the gate verdicts once they conclude.

- **Public surface** — `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` gains `.strict()`; its `.describe` is rewritten. The members (`id` min 1, `name` optional min 1) and the exported type are unchanged, and `z.input` still equals `z.infer` (strictness adds no default or transform), so the `Iso_api_protocol__MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` pin and the 799 count stand. The only observable narrowing is on an unknown member of `client`: stripped at `6ef6a96021`, refused now. That member was never published as accepted, no consumer exists yet (the cloud door is a follow-up), and the in-process writer already refused it — so the published-surface effect is to make the spec say what the writer did. **Right.**
- **Writer** — `authoringClientOf` now delegates to `MetadataAuthoringClientSchema.safeParse` and returns `parsed.data`, so the save door (`protocol.ts` ~20245) and the stored read (`storedDraftChanges`) judge a client by the spec's own verdict, one source. `safeParse` of a strict object returns the declared members only, so the stored form is unchanged. `isPlainObject` keeps its two other callers. The `6ef6a96021` writer tests (`{ id, secret }` refused, `metadataWrites()` empty) are untouched and still describe the behaviour. **Right.**
- **Generated artifacts** — `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` carries the new describe. `json-schema.manifest/api.json` is a name list (`api/MetadataAuthoringClient`, unchanged) and the strictness count for `api/` is an object-site total that a posture change does not move (`strictness-ledger.ts`: sites are counted, posture is classified), so neither needed a regen in this commit. `api-surface` / `export-origins` / `declaration-map` / `authorable-surface` carry no posture and are unchanged. **Right**, pending the in-progress Lint lanes (`check:generated`, `check:strictness-ledger`).
- No accept-set change on the HTTP doors, no new export, no ADR touched.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from `6ef6a96021`: spec minor, metadata-protocol minor, rest and console packages patch; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added` on both PR body and changeset. The delta refuses an unknown member on a schema that first ships in this same release, so nothing published on `main` is narrowed and no arm or banner changes. **Matches.** `Check Changeset` is in progress.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `open_questions` and no dev flag in the delta or on the card.
- `.strict()` is the spelling this file already uses (two sites at the head); no gate prefers the campaign's `strictObject(` helper, and the `api/` ledger is untriaged, so no verdict row is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, judged against the two findings of the `6ef6a96021` record and the writer it cites.

- **Should-fix closed.** The spec and the writer now give one verdict on an unknown member: the schema is `.strict()` ("refused, never stripped" in its describe), and `authoringClientOf` parses through it instead of holding a second shape check. `meta-item-response-shapes.test.ts` pins `{ id: 'cli_1', secret: 's' }` refused at `draftChanges[0].client`, so the spec's own test now carries the row the writer test carried alone. Contract-first holds (Prime Directive #12: the contract owned at the spec, the consumer applying it).
- **Nit closed.** The describe no longer names its own schema; it now says what the client is (the consented client, as the door verified it from the token) and that it is closed.
- Tried to break it: a stored `mcp` entry whose client carries an extra member (hand-edited row) is still dropped as malformed by `storedDraftChanges`, now by the spec's verdict; a served draft read therefore never carries a client the schema would refuse, so any response-side parse against `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` keeps passing. An in-process caller that passes a client with a stray member is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST` exactly as before. Nothing new on the spec face.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-e4rirs`
Reviewed-by: `session_0123kRqqdpAJWYMgsgdAJX4G`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Seat review (`repo:cloud#2`, routed `domain:cloud`): ACCEPT** (head `2b1028a55a`, 2026-10-28T11:19Z)

- **Contract review:** PASS at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on `6ef6a96021`. The delta to `2b1028a55a` closes the should-fix (`MetadataAuthoringClientSchema` is now `.strict()`, and the writer parses through it) and the nit, also PASS. Both records are on this PR. `needs:contract-review` is removed.
- **Rest of the diff at TIER_DEFAULT:**
  - `metadata-protocol`: the draft save records `surface: 'mcp'` plus `client`, accepted only from an in-process caller with surface `mcp`. Anything else is refused 400 before any write.
  - `rest` and `runtime`: `?surface=mcp` is refused on both HTTP doors through the shared closed set.
  - `ui`: `StudioDraftMark` and `DraftChangesPanel` render the surface and client, in all 10 locales for the drawer and en/zh for the designer table. The new tests pin both.
- **Governed:** no. 870 lines.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, spec minor. They match the diff.

Landing via queue once every check on this head is green, not just the required subset. The cloud half (the MCP door passes `surface: 'mcp'` and the client into the save) follows the pin round that carries this. cloud#3302 stays open until then.

**Seat 2 review: ACCEPT carried to head `532985f`** (2026-10-28T12:00Z)

The only change since the ACCEPT at `2b1028a55a` is test-only. It moves the two `de-quote-pairing-3876.test.ts` pins from 97 to 98 for the new correctly paired `preview.changes.draftedByMcpClient` string, and the de string itself is unchanged. No `packages/spec/src/**` file changed, so contract review record2 (delta PASS) still covers the spec diff. Every check on `532985f` is green or skipped.

Landing via queue.
